name: Automation
blurb: Workflows and browsers that run themselves safely: n8n, Make, Zapier, Playwright, DevTools, app CLIs and web extraction.
searches: n8n MCP workflow skill new release
Zapier SDK durable workflows agent skill
browser automation CLI for AI agents new

tests.prompt: When someone fills in our feedback form, I want AI to score the sentiment and post the negative ones to our team chat. Build it in Make.
tests.good: Asks which form tool, which AI provider and which chat app before choosing modules; discovers modules via apps_recommend (one app per call) and app_modules_list; presents the flow (e.g. If-Else or filter) and a Scenario Plan for confirmation; lists connections with scope status and has the user pick even if only one exists; validates modules and blueprint, uses 'immediately' scheduling for a webhook trigger, activates, verifies output content, and has the user send a real test submission rather than echoing the webhook URL.

tests.prompt: Our Playwright checkout test fails about one run in five on CI. Fix it.
tests.good: Reads the trace/failure first; reproduces with --debug=cli and playwright-cli attach (PLAYWRIGHT_HTML_OPEN=never); looks for timing causes (fixed sleeps, networkidle, assertions before data loads, shared state between tests, third-party calls); replaces them with role-based locators, web-first assertions and mocked external requests; keeps the assertion strength; reruns repeatedly to confirm stability and reports any real app bug found.

tests.prompt: Build an n8n workflow: Stripe webhook for refunds -> append a row to Google Sheets -> post a Slack message if the refund is over $500.
tests.good: Uses webhook data under $json.body, verifies the Stripe signature or a secret, responds quickly; discovers nodes and current typeVersions; omits placeholder credentials and has the user confirm credentials per node; dedupes on refund ID; compares amounts in cents; validates, reads back connections, tests with pinned data asking before real Slack posts; adds an error workflow, descriptive node names and description; activates only after testing and gives a handoff note.

tests.prompt: Every Monday morning, check the prices of the 40 products we track on three supplier websites, append them to our Google Sheet, and email me any that moved more than 5%. Run it in the cloud as a small script, not on my laptop.
tests.good: States a short plan first: automation-design.md, web-extraction.md and app-integrations.md here (a supplier feed or API before a browser; robots.txt and terms respected; throttled); the sheet through docs-office (google-workspace.md: gws with the fewest scopes, schema checked before sheets +append); the schedule through cloud-devops (gcp.md: a Cloud Run job on Cloud Scheduler, credentials from Secret Manager). Confirms the plan with run time and timezone; dedupes per product and week; drafts the email or asks before the first real send; adds an error path that tells a human; checks the Done means of all three crafts.

tests.prompt: Our team lives in Microsoft 365. Every Friday I want a flow that reads new rows from a SharePoint list called Project Tasks, emails the project owner a summary of overdue items, and posts a count in a Teams channel. Build it in Power Automate and tell me how to test it without spamming people.
tests.good: Names Power Automate cloud flows and uses a Recurrence (scheduled) trigger with an explicit time zone, not a polling item-created trigger; uses the SharePoint Get items action with an OData filter on due date and Status, handling pagination (threshold and top count); uses Office 365 Outlook and Teams connectors with connections the user picks or signs in to, with no credentials in the flow; creates and tests the flow stopped or in a test environment, sends test mail to the user only, and confirms before turning the flow on; adds error handling (Configure run after, scope with a failure notification) and notes the licensing or connector limits; mentions the official Power Automate plugin or az login route only as an option and never asks for tenant secrets in chat.

tools.name: n8n
tools.why: One of the four largest general-purpose workflow platforms in 2026 round-ups (digidop, automationatlas) with an official Claude connector and a built-in instance-level MCP server.

tools.name: Zapier
tools.why: Original market leader with 8,000-9,000+ app connectors in every 2026 comparison and an Anthropic-verified Claude connector (Zapier MCP).

tools.name: Make
tools.why: Third of the big three no-code platforms in every 2026 comparison (digidop, automationatlas); has a hosted Make MCP server and a Claude connector.

tools.name: Playwright
tools.why: State of JS 2025 'Most Adopted' testing tool (about 52% usage, 91% satisfaction) and about 33M weekly npm downloads; Microsoft ships a CLI skill and an official MCP server.

tools.name: Microsoft Power Automate
tools.why: Named as one of the four largest workflow platforms in 2026 round-ups (automationatlas), bundled with Microsoft 365; Microsoft now publishes an official Power Automate plugin for Claude Code (Learn doc dated Sept 2026).

tools.name: UiPath
tools.why: RPA market leader: a Leader in the Gartner Magic Quadrant for RPA for the seventh year running (2025, highest Ability to Execute) and the most adopted RPA platform at scale (about 23.5% RPA share in industry stats); UiPath ships an official `uip` CLI with coding-agent skills for Claude Code (UiPath/skills, MIT).

tools.name: GitHub Actions
tools.why: Leading CI/CD and repo-automation platform: 33% of organisations and 62% of personal projects in the JetBrains 2025 ecosystem survey, and the usual way to run scheduled scripts and Claude Code itself (claude-code-action).

tools.name: Selenium
tools.why: Still the enterprise backbone for browser automation (about 2.1M weekly npm downloads, 7 languages) per State of JS 2025 coverage and the tech-insider comparison.

tools.name: Google Apps Script
tools.why: The free, default way to automate Gmail, Sheets, Docs, Forms and Calendar triggers (mail merge samples, time-driven triggers, clasp CLI); 2026 quotas include 30-minute runs and 1,500 recipients a day (automationatlas, Google samples).

tools.name: Puppeteer
tools.why: Long-standing Chrome/Firefox automation library for scraping and PDF generation (about 95k GitHub stars); common in existing scripts users ask to fix.

tools.name: Apify
tools.why: Leading managed scraping platform with thousands of ready-made Actors, a hosted MCP server at mcp.apify.com and a Claude desktop connector.

tools.name: Firecrawl
tools.why: Popular scrape/crawl/search API that returns clean markdown, with an official MCP server and a skills repo.

tools.name: Browserbase
tools.why: Hosted headless-browser infrastructure plus the Stagehand framework; its skills repo has about 3.7k stars.

tools.name: Pipedream
tools.why: Developer-first workflow platform (about 11.7k GitHub stars, 2,000+ apps, code steps) with a remote MCP server.

tools.name: Composio
tools.why: Integration broker with hundreds of apps and managed OAuth for agents; official skills repo.

tools.name: Chrome DevTools MCP
tools.why: Google's official MCP server for driving and debugging Chrome (about 53k GitHub stars).

tools.name: Automation Anywhere
tools.why: Second-largest RPA vendor (about 18% enterprise share in industry stats) and a Leader in the 2025 Gartner Magic Quadrant for RPA alongside UiPath, Blue Prism and Power Automate; no usable agent skills yet.

tools.name: Workato
tools.why: Leader in the 2025 Gartner Magic Quadrant for iPaaS (with Boomi) and the usual enterprise answer in 2026 workflow-tool round-ups; docs now cover Enterprise MCP and third-party agents. Enterprise-only, so minor.

tools.name: IFTTT
tools.why: Largest consumer automation service (27-32 million users, 1,000+ connected products per IFTTT's own pages); common for personal and smart-home triggers, little use for business workflows and no agent skills.
